reference_materials: Native closed-tool product photo and all three use photos viewed
Native adjustable-joint and internal-opening-spring cutaway viewed
findings: Eight final browser views were inspected: closed/open top and oblique views, head top/oblique and internal-joint top/oblique. The original manufacturer images are not redistributed.

The candidate retains crossed forged levers, a curved polished head, two crimp recesses, an adjustable pivot, small retainer wheel and tapered red coated grips. Rounded outer jaws, real blade bevels, edge chamfers and circular bolt end faces replace the initial flat polygonal prototype.

The internal view hides explicitly named parts and clips distant geometry. The spring occupies an actual recess around the pivot bore; it does not pass through the steel. This view is not an assembly sequence.

Full steel grip cores and separate thin coatings replace a mostly-plastic initial hypothesis. The selected density estimate is about 311 g against the 310 g catalogue value. Density, coating profile, centre of mass and inertia are still inferred.

Actual rigid resting contacts include both grips and the pivot fastener. The inferred mass-centre range stays inside their support polygon with at least 13 mm margin; this establishes a static staged reference only.
Metric and US width differences remain explicit. The roughly 44.9 mm closed width is a photo/US interpretation; the 60 mm metric envelope has unspecified jaw state.
geometry_limits: Not manufacturer CAD or measured surface reconstruction. Local head, blade, crimp, neck, grip and fastener profiles remain hypotheses; commercial markings and textures are not copied.
The spring has no validated ends, preload or stiffness. The small retainer has no qualified locking contact; blade severing, crimping, force, deformation and robot grasp remain open.
Nine independent intermediate geometric states and a 3 mm wire entry do not establish continuous motion or material compatibility. The source 5 mm wire-rope and 6 mm copper-cable rows are distinct.
